Key Highlights:

  • Plans to close ~70 additional underperforming stores in Q3 and Q4, bringing total planned closures to ~120 in fiscal 2026.

data.title: Stocks Are Resilient, Fairly Priced, and Probably Getting Ready to Rally — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Alex Rosenberg

The stock market aced two big tests this week. That's a great sign for its resilience-and suggests that the next meaningful move could take stocks higher.

The first test came Monday, when investors grappled with the idea that frontier artificial-intelligence companies Anthropic and OpenAI might intentionally slow their own progress to save the human race from a murderous superintelligence.

That sounds less like a stock market headline than the plot of a 1953 monster movie. But Anthropic CEO Dario Amodio really did write a bracing Sept. 12 note entitled "We Must Pace the Frontier" in which he argued that AI companies should slow development for safety reasons. Strikingly, he also called for broad regulation of the AI industry. Not wanting to be left out, Microsoft announced Monday that it was adding more guardrails around its AI development.

These developments came a few days after Anthropic (and ex-OpenAI) researcher Jacob Coxon resigned with a public declaration that neither Anthropic nor OpenAI is acting responsibly. "The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade," he wrote.

If AI developers tap the brakes, they certainly won't need to buy as many chips as quickly. So on Monday, the iShares Semiconductor exchange-traded fund plunged 5.6% for its worst session in two months, embarrassing any columnists who might have recently published bullish takes on chips. But the "pacing" narrative quickly cooled off, and the ETF rose for four days straight to end the week flat.

The market seems to be coalescing around the narrative BofA Securities semiconductor analyst Vivek Arya put forward on Monday morning. "The economic stakes are simply too large for any sustained meaningful deceleration," he wrote, adding that since Washington is unlikely to regulate the industry, he expects "any eventual outcome to resemble industry-led self-regulation, akin to Finra (finance) [or] MPA (movies)." (Perhaps the next iteration of Claude will get a little warning label: "This model is rated p(doom)-17, for graphic threats to human existence.")

The second test came on Wednesday, when the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate for the first time in three years.

Stocks barely reacted to the decision, but as Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh began to explain his thinking, the S&P 500 index tanked. "I would be hard-pressed to describe broad financial conditions as restrictive," Warsh said. "This view was widely shared by the Committee. So we removed a dose of accommodation."

Since Warsh opts to say so little, every word he utters is subjected to Talmudic analysis. In this case, the idea that a hike merely removes a dose of accommodation was taken to mean that policy remains accommodative even after this hike. Since policy probably shouldn't be accommodative when the economy is running at full employment and above-target inflation, the clear implication is that Warsh won't hesitate to raise rates even higher so as to remove yet more of these metaphorical doses.

Things got weird when CNBC's Steve Liesman asked Warsh where the federal-funds rate is relative to the so-called neutral rate-the policy rate that is neither accommodative nor restrictive. Warsh answered that while he finds the idea of a neutral rate interesting "as an academic matter," the concept doesn't have "an operational effect on decisions that we make today."

It's a puzzling stance. "How do you say we 'removed a dose of accommodation' without having a neutral rate in mind?" wrote economist Claudia Sahm. "It is the dividing line between accommodation and restriction."

Cynics-and Wall Street is glutted with them-might say this is all by design. Some argue that Warsh wants to keep the economy balanced by effectively delivering a spate of rate hikes, but without earning President Donald Trump's ire, which explains why he eschews forward guidance but finds artful means of implying that more hikes are ahead.

Either way, the market soon thought better of the afternoon swoon, and the S&P 500 surged 1.14% on Thursday for its best session in more than a month. And why not? Even if the Fed hikes two more times this year, the impact on S&P 500 companies is likely to be limited. They are much less reliant on debt, since they've reduced their ratio of net debt to Ebitda (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization) from 1.7 a decade ago to 1.3 today. And their earnings growth, at around 26%, remains staggering. What matters more than the path of short-term rates is whether the Fed can maintain its credibility and enhance its ability to respond to any future recessions; on Wednesday, Warsh's Fed took the right step in both directions.

It probably hasn't escaped your attention that the S&P 500 has traded in a narrow 3.2% range since Aug. 4. This has been a healthy period of consolidation and has allowed the S&P 500's forward price/earnings ratio to come down from 20.3 at the start of that period (and 22.2 at the start of the year) to 19.2 today, per FactSet data. "Because equity prices have failed to keep pace with surging earnings, near-term valuations show no hint of a bubble," writes Goldman Sachs Chief U.S. Equity Strategist Ben Snider.

This means the stock market could be gathering its strength for a surge to fresh highs. Just so long as earnings keep up their strength-and the Robot Monster remains at bay.

Write to Alex Rosenberg at alex.rosenberg@barrons.com

data.description:

Von Hertzen had been serving as interim CFO. Trading in WISA shares on Nasdaq Helsinki is expected to begin on November 2, 2026, following the demerger's completion on October 31.

WISA's planned leadership team will include President and CEO Tuija Suur-Hamari, CFO von Hertzen, and other senior executives.

On the Frankfurt stock exchange, shares of UPM-Kymmene were gaining 0.53 percent, changing hands at 26.32 euros.

data.title: EU wheat tracks Chicago lower as Black Sea uncertainty lingers
data.description:
Euronext wheat fell for a second session on Friday in step with Chicago prices while traders continued to assess the impact of war disruption to Black Sea exports from Russia and Ukraine.

December wheat on Euronext settled 0.8% lower at €241.50 ($277.07) a metric ton after the day session.

The contract was almost unchanged over the week.

Chicago wheat fell about 2%, with the US market facing additional pressure from a seven-week high for the dollar index .

Wheat markets have been choppy this week as investors have reacted to diplomatic efforts to achieve de-escalation in Russia's war with Ukraine, ongoing military strikes in the Black Sea zone, and signs that Russian and Ukrainian wheat was still reaching markets.

“The market is torn between hopes of a diplomatic agreement for Black Sea safe shipping against the reality that Russian and Ukrainian attacks continue every day,” one German trader said.

Shipments of about 30,000 tons of Russian wheat for sale on Friday included one loading in St Petersburg offered at $275 a ton free on board (FOB), two in Ust-Luga at $280 and $275, and five from ports in Latvia at between $275 and $280 a ton FOB, traders said.

“Today alone I saw sales offers for around 220,000 tons of Russian 12.5% wheat for October shipment from Baltic ports," the trader said. "It is difficult to guess volumes of Russian wheat coming onto the market from the Baltic but it is naturally way below levels of over 1 million tons a week previously in the Black Sea.”

The ongoing Russian flows have tempered reaction to demand this week from major importers Algeria and Pakistan.

($1 = 0.8716 euros)

data.title: Vijay’s UK Visit Brings Rs 15,300 Crore Investment Commitments To Tamil Nadu
data.description:
The commitments span automotive manufacturing, GCCs, renewable energy and power equipment, with more than 10,000 jobs expected

Tamil Nadu Says CM Vijay’s UK Visit Secures Rs 15,300 Crore Investment Commitments

Chennai, 18 September 2026: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay’s recent visit to the United Kingdom resulted in investment commitments worth Rs 15,300 crore and the potential to create more than 10,000 direct and indirect jobs, according to the state government. The six-day visit was part of the government’s strategy to attract global investment and support its target of building a USD 1.5 trillion economy by 2036.

The investment commitments span automotive components, engineering, manufacturing, renewable energy, power equipment and Global Capability Centres (GCCs). The government said the latest commitments add to more than Rs 1 lakh crore in investments attracted during the first 100 days of the government.

Auto And Technology Investments

On 14 September, Samvardhana Motherson International, along with its European and UK-based joint venture partners, committed approximately Rs 11,000 crore towards chassis, engineering, manufacturing, assembly and warehousing facilities in Tamil Nadu. The project is expected to generate around 7,000 jobs.

A European auto component manufacturer also submitted a Letter of Intent identifying Tamil Nadu as its preferred destination for a proposed Rs 3,000 crore investment in India.

In the technology and services sector, Ernst & Young (EY) signed an agreement to establish a GCC under the Build-Operate-Transform-Transfer model along the proposed Mount-Poonamallee GCC corridor in Chennai. The project involves an investment of Rs 1,000 crore and is expected to create around 2,000 jobs.

Swedish Sigma Technology Group is also set to expand its GCC presence in Tiruchirappalli and Chennai through its Indian arm Sreeya Solutions, with around 600 jobs expected in embedded systems and electrification. UK-based Wilson Power Solutions has committed Rs 300 crore towards a facility in Tiruvallur, with around 400 employment opportunities expected.

Trade And Industry Engagement

During the visit, Vijay met Indian High Commissioner to the UK Kumaran Periasamy in London on 12 September to discuss trade opportunities arising from the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement.

The Chief Minister also met executives of the Hinduja Group, including Ashok Leyland MD Dheeraj Hinduja and Finolex Industries MD Prakash P Chhabria. The executives briefed him on progress related to a Rs 2,500 crore MoU signed during the VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investors Conclave 2026. The group also expressed interest in expanding investments in renewable energy, particularly wind power, and increasing exports of commercial vehicles manufactured in Tamil Nadu.

The state government said the VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investors Conclave had resulted in 97 MoUs worth Rs 67,452 crore, with the potential to create 1,06,998 jobs.

Motor Sports And Future Partnerships

As part of the visit, Vijay inspected the Silverstone Motor Racing Circuit in connection with Tamil Nadu’s proposed Motor Sports City. He reviewed the circuit’s race control, safety and operational facilities and flagged off the 2026 Michelin Le Mans Cup race, in which actor and racing driver Ajith Kumar participated.

The state government also said discussions during the visit covered raw material procurement for Tamil Nadu’s jewellery and textile manufacturers, a proposed UK aerospace and defence delegation to Hosur, a Northern England space delegation’s planned visit to Chennai, and skill development partnerships in financial services.

The government said the visit also explored opportunities to strengthen UK-Tamil Nadu trade and investment ties across multiple sectors.

data.title: Prasanna Kumar Acharya Takes Charge As CMD Of NLC India
data.description:
Nearly three decades of experience across power, mining, infrastructure and finance leadership roles in India shape his new mandate today

Dr. Prasanna Kumar Acharya has taken charge as Chairman-cum-Managing Director (CMD) of NLC India, succeeding to the top leadership position at the energy and mining company. He assumed office on 17 September 2026 at the company’s Corporate Office in Neyveli.

Acharya brings nearly three decades of professional experience across the power, mining and infrastructure sectors. Before taking charge as CMD, he served as Director (Finance) at NLC India, giving him experience of the company’s financial operations and business activities.

Career Across Key Sectors

Acharya’s professional career includes senior roles at GRIDCO, NTPC, Tata Power and NLC India. His experience spans power generation, transmission and distribution, mining and metro rail infrastructure.

His career has included responsibilities across different segments of the energy and infrastructure ecosystem, along with senior finance functions. His previous role as Director (Finance) at NLC India provided exposure to the company’s financial and operational priorities before his elevation to the CMD position.

Finance Leadership At NLC

As Director (Finance), Acharya was part of the senior leadership at NLC India, with responsibilities linked to the company’s financial function.

His wider professional experience includes work across public-sector and private-sector organisations in the power and infrastructure space. The combination of finance experience and sector exposure forms part of his professional background as he takes on the CMD role.

Academic Qualifications

Acharya holds a B.Com (Honours) from Utkal University and an LLB from M.S. Law College, Cuttack. He also holds a Master of Commerce from Ravenshaw University and an MBA.

His academic background combines commerce, law and management, alongside his professional experience in finance and infrastructure.

New Leadership Mandate

NLC India operates across the power and mining value chain, making the CMD position central to the company’s overall management and business direction.

Acharya’s appointment marks a leadership transition at the company, with his previous experience in finance and his broader exposure to power, mining and infrastructure forming the foundation of his new role.

data.title: Mozambique says IMF mission may open way for new loan programme
data.description:
Mozambique’s finance ministry said on Friday it hoped an International Monetary Fund mission that ended this week would pave the way for a new support programme, while the fund suggested more reforms may need to come first.

The ministry said in a statement that there could be a follow-up mission, possibly in November, to discuss programme conditions and targets.

The IMF said in an end-of-mission statement that talks on "the reforms needed to pave the way for a Fund-supported program" would continue in the coming months.

Mozambique’s dollar bond maturing in September 2031 pared earlier gains after the IMF statement and was bid at 94.29 cents, Tradeweb data showed.

The September 9 to 18 mission, led by IMF mission chief Pablo Lopez-Murphy, met Prime Minister Maria Benvinda Levi, Finance Minister Carla Loveira and Central Bank Governor Felisberto Navalha.

The resource-rich Southern African nation's previous IMF programme ended early in April 2025, with talks for a new deal expected to hinge on economic reforms.

The fund said economic activity "remains subdued but is showing signs of recovery", with inflation contained and fiscal consolidation that began in 2025 continuing, anchored by spending restraint.

One of Mozambique's most pressing challenges remains its heavy debt burden, which a World Bank and International Monetary Fund analysis has deemed unsustainable.

Its problems date back to a 2016 hidden-debt scandal, which wrecked investor confidence and curbed access to funding.

Delays to major natural gas projects that had been expected to boost exports, revenue and government finances have made matters worse.

Earlier this year, Mozambique cleared its outstanding obligation with the IMF, a move analysts said would strengthen its case for fresh funding.

data.title: Netflix Stock Falls After Downgrade. Why It's Losing the Streaming Wars to Disney. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By George Glover

Netflix desperately needs to find the next Squid Game. The video streamer is struggling to churn out hits-and that's dire news for its shares, which have already taken a battering in 2026.

The stock dropped 4.4% to $72.02 in early trading. It was already down about 20% for the year through Thursday's close.

The catalyst for the selloff was a downgrade. Wells Fargo analyst Steven Cahall lowered his rating for Netflix to Underweight and slashed his price target to $57 from $80.

The new price target implies shares could slump another 25%.

Netflix stunned investors in July when it said it would would start publishing its flagship engagement report once instead of twice a year, fueling fears that it's bleeding subscribers to rival streamers.

"Engagement trends look worrying to us," Cahall wrote in a research note. "Netflix has lacked big original series and it's showing...We see breakout hits as a must for the stock to work again."

Disney looks like a "more hit-driven" streamer right now, he added.

There are ways for Netflix to stop the rot. It could plow more money into content, license more live sports content, or look to grow via mergers and acquisitions. The streamer agreed to buy Warner Bros. Discovery late last year, but lost a bidding war to Paramount Skydance.

Any of those options would probably create a "messier Netflix story" for investors, Cahall said. The analyst's $57 price target values Netflix stock at about 15-times expected earnings per share for 2027, compared with around 20 times as of Thursday's close.

Netflix didn't immediately respond to a request for comment Friday.
